clue.text: Basket case's beginning to feel senses wobble

indicators.note: the beginning of the word case is its opening letter, which starts the answer

parts.note: to reel is to feel one's senses swim or stagger

explanation.surface: A nervous wreck starts to feel giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Basket'; 'case's beginning' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket, typically one an angler uses to carry fish.

clue.text: Bodies in motion in lively callisthenics came with added energy

indicators.note: lively movement of the letters signals that they are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Gym exercises arrive with an extra burst of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with added' joins E for energy to the pool; 'lively' shakes up CALLISTHENICS, CAME and E together.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial mechanics is the branch of astronomy studying how heavenly bodies such as planets move under gravity.

clue.text: None mute sex when active? Everyone clear off

indicators.note: once these letters are set in motion they rearrange themselves into the answer

explanation.surface: A sexless, silent crowd is told to leave the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt omnes is the Latin stage direction meaning all the actors leave the stage.

clue.text: See spades perhaps I dropped after turning over flower

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: turning over means the letters left are read backwards in this down entry
the letter I is let fall out of the card word

parts.note: spades is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at a garden spade and then flip it over to find a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is the old exclamation lo; 'spades' is the card suit, not garden tools. 'I dropped' and 'turning over' act on the suit in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Adaptation of Dune left many without excitement

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks the original, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film version of the novel Dune bored a lot of viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mundanely means doing it in a dull, ordinary, unexciting way.

clue.text: My staff reduced almost everything — that's obscure

indicators.note: reduced tells us the walking-staff word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stick is a staff used for walking

indicators.note: almost the whole word means it stops one letter short

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone's workforce has been cut back to almost nothing, which is hard to fathom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a walking stick; 'reduced' and 'almost' each cut one letter, giving STIC and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mystical has a hidden spiritual meaning, so it is obscure to ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Restraining expression of disgust is not nothing

indicators.note: the negative word holds the cry of disgust in its grip, around it

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Holding back a groan of revulsion amounts to nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is the figure zero, another word for nothing.

clue.text: Amended moral bias is delectable

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Correcting one's moral prejudice is a delightful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosial means fit for the gods, like ambrosia, so delicious or delightful.

clue.text: European with energy and self-confidence

parts.note: go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A dynamic, self-assured person from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy' here is not E (that came from 'European') but GO, as in get-up-and-go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of self-worth or self-esteem.

clue.text: Large part of Canada that may accommodate European country

indicators.note: the dialect word for that gives room to the country inside it

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that
UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A vast Canadian region might have room for a whole European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukon is a large territory in north-west Canada.

clue.text: Scenery material recalled character in Hamlet

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a set is the scenery for a play
material can mean real or physical

explanation.surface: Stage scenery was brought back to mind for a role in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a noun (fabric for a set) but is the adjective REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, who duels with the prince at the end.

clue.text: No ball carried by university rugby forward, that's clear

indicators.note: the cricket abbreviation is borne along inside the other letters

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
NB is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a no ball

explanation.surface: A student rugby forward picks up a no ball in a mix of sports.
explanation.walkthrough: NB stands for a no ball, an illegal delivery in cricket; a lock is a rugby second-row forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock something is to clear an obstruction from it.

clue.text: Wrong indicator? Not good

indicators.note: not good says the word for good has to go from the indicator word

parts.note: a sign is an indicator

explanation.surface: A faulty signal on a car? It's no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrong, a moral offence.

clue.text: Museum to fashion youngster — Scots boy — with instant education I promoted

parts.note: to smith is to fashion metal by forging
a son is a youngster
Ian is a Scottish boy's name
inst. is an old abbreviation for instant, meaning this month in letters

indicators.note: promoted means the letter is moved up to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: tuition is education

explanation.surface: A museum aims to shape a young Scot by giving him an education right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant' is the old letter-writing abbreviation for this month; 'I promoted' means the letter I is moved up to the front of the education word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Smithsonian Institution in Washington DC runs a group of national museums.

clue.text: Fake misattributed in the auction, not old

indicators.note: a misattributed letter is put in the wrong place, so these letters are rearranged
not old tells us that the letter for old is left out of the words

explanation.surface: A forgery wrongly credited to a master turns up at the sale, and it is not antique.
explanation.definitionFit: Inauthentic means not genuine, so a fake is inauthentic.

clue.text: Absolutely guaranteed college boy can join club

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A student can be admitted to a club with no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can join' just links the pieces; the club, written last in the clue, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironclad guarantee is one that is completely secure and cannot be broken.

clue.text: Frank and Bill with yen for standing for office

parts.note: candid means frank
a/c, short for account, is a bill
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Two men, Frank and Bill, with a longing, run for election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank and Bill' look like two men's names; 'yen' looks like a longing but is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidacy is the state of being a candidate, standing for election to a post.

clue.text: Lot of team taken aback, with member put on the back foot

indicators.note: taken aback is read as taken backwards, reversing the letters
a lot of the word, not all, means it loses its last letter

parts.note: a side is a team
an arm is a member, a limb

explanation.surface: Most of a squad were startled when one player was forced onto the defensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of' trims SIDE to SID, and 'taken aback' turns it to DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm an opponent is to take away their weapons or advantage, leaving them on the defensive.

clue.text: See 1
Algebraic quantity that may work to contain two bits of arithmetic

indicators.note: the word for workable holds the two letters inside it

parts.note: viable means capable of working or succeeding

indicators.note: the two bits taken are the opening pair of letters of the word

explanation.surface: An unknown in algebra that might succeed if it holds a bit of sums.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra a variable is a symbol such as x standing for a quantity that can change.

clue.text: Adding warmth to connection lacking heart

indicators.note: lacking heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: linking is a connection between things

explanation.surface: Bringing some warmth to a relationship that has lost its emotional core.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining a coat or curtain adds an inner layer that makes it warmer.

clue.text: Live movement capturing a couple of lines related to dance

indicators.note: the word for live holds the next letters captive inside it

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A live performance includes a pair of verses connected to dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like dance motion but is a twitch, TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletic means of or like ballet, a theatrical form of dance.

clue.text: Appointed grandma to dismiss a chaperone

parts.note: due means appointed or scheduled, as in the due time

indicators.note: dismiss means send away, so one A is sent out of the word

parts.note: nana is a familiar word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother is given the job of seeing off a chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as chaperone to a young girl, especially in Spain.

clue.text: See 12
Be charged in court, wasting time, nothing less

indicators.note: nothing less means the letter for zero is taken away
wasting time means the letter for time is lost from the word

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A defendant is charged in court after a long delay, no less.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to have it charged to you.

clue.text: Conan Doyle hero — name set to enthral one

indicators.note: enthral is taken as hold within, so the name and setting words together hold the numeral

parts.note: to gel is to set
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Conan Doyle hero's name is bound to captivate a reader.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Holmes: Sir Nigel Loring is the knight hero of Conan Doyle's historical novels The White Company and Sir Nigel.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle wrote a novel titled Sir Nigel about the knight Nigel Loring.

clue.text: What follows a do, back in time

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale re follows do, so what follows a do is a re

explanation.surface: The aftermath of a party, back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party, but it is the note of the sol-fa scale, which re follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, a span of time.

clue.text: Better money required to secure a team leader

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: the slang word for cash locks the letter safely inside it

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: More cash is needed to sign up a club captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain is the player who leads a sports team.

clue.text: Small amount of coal? It's a lot of fuel

indicators.note: a lot of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: peat is a fuel dug from bogs

explanation.surface: A little coal? That's plenty of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea coal is a grade of coal in small pieces, each about the size of a pea.

clue.text: Italian car designer upset at odd bits of trim

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy or upset them

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A car designer is upset by stray bits of trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but is BUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettore Bugatti was an Italian-born designer who founded the Bugatti car company.

clue.text: Prepared in advance to study old article about crackpot

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: about means the old article goes around the crazy word

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the definite article the
mad means crazy, like a crackpot

explanation.surface: Someone got ready early to research an antique piece on an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are produced beforehand rather than to order.

clue.text: Endless source of devastation in place

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: locust swarms devastate crops

explanation.surface: A never-ending source of ruin sits in one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place, used for a position or site in maths and law.
